M1.reason: All six views and the four close angles match the original's outline. Measured overlap is 0.969 to 0.982, and nothing sticks out or is missing in the side, back or top views. The coat hem differs slightly in the back and side views, but not enough to change the silhouette.

M2.reason: Measured size is 33.3 x 21.5 x 68 against the original's 33.3 x 21.7 x 68. Every dimension is within 1%, well inside 10%.

M3.reason: All parts are present in the right places and shapes: glasses, grey hair, bald crown, shirt, patterned tie, belt, white coat with lapels, trousers, brown shoes, both hands and arms. The counts match. The coat hem reads a little differently at the back, but the component itself is there.

M4.reason: The mean colour difference of 8.1 passes the line of 15, but the picture shows clear differences the mean hides. In the below view the reproduction has tan and skin-toned patches and brown blotches where the original is dark. Its per-view figure there is 16.8, over 15. The coat also carries grey-brown grime blotches at the lower back and front-left that the original's clean white cloth does not have. The skin, glasses, shoes and tie do match.

M5.reason: The original's folds, the belt, shirt and tie are all there, but the reproduction adds grime and wear the original does not show: dark blotches on the coat's lower back and streaks at the hem. That is added wrong detail, so it cannot score 2.

M6.reason: At game size the figure reads as the same scientist, but a player who knows him would notice the mottled, dirty-looking coat, the odd split or flare at the hem from the back and side, and the tan patches on the underside. Those are enough to say it is not the original.

M7.reason: The front faces the same way as the original, the figure stands upright, and its feet sit on the same ground line in the front, side and back views.

M8.reason: SMAK's checks returned no errors. The reproduction has 700 triangles against the original's 740, well under the 2x limit. Nothing visibly floats or is inside out in any view. The underside is the closest call, but it shows no open holes that the checks would miss.

C1.reason: In the run, the figure stays on its body in most frames, but in several frames (3/22, 9/22, 13/22, 22/22) the coat tail flares out as a separate sheet and the shoes sit away from the trouser ends with visible gaps, so they look like they float or come loose from the legs. The original's coat tail and feet move with the legs. The judge cannot see the stunt test in these pictures, so C1 is scored on the run alone.
